title: We’re co-leading the European Heritage Hub’s new digital task force
content:
We are proud to announce that we will be co-leading the newly launched Digital Task Force of the EU-funded European Heritage Hub, alongside the Europeana Foundation. This Task Force brings together members of the European Heritage Alliance to tackle one of the most defining challenges facing the cultural heritage sector today: ensuring that digital transformation remains ethical, inclusive, sustainable, and above all, people-centred.

From high-resolution imaging and 3D reconstruction to sensors and artificial intelligence, digital technologies are unlocking new possibilities to document, preserve, research and share cultural heritage. But technology on its own is not the goal. As co-leads of this Task Force, we believe digital tools must remain in service of the sector, complementing, not replacing, the expertise of heritage professionals and the knowledge held by communities.

This conviction sits at the heart of everything the Digital Task Force will pursue.

title: Celebrating Europe’s Sporting Heritage: A Successful International Conference in Zagreb
content:
On 12 September 2026, the My Sporting Heritage project celebrated an important milestone with its international conference, “Preserving and Promoting Europe’s Sporting Heritage”. Hosted at the Technical Museum Nikola Tesla in Zagreb, Croatia, the event brought together experts, researchers, educators, museums, sport organisations and cultural heritage professionals from across Europe and beyond.

Participants also joined online, making the conference an inclusive opportunity for international exchange.

Organised by Radiona.org – Zagreb Makerspace and Sport & Citoyenneté, on behalf of the whole My Sporting Heritage consortium, the conference provided an opportunity to reflect on the value of sporting heritage and explore innovative ways to preserve, interpret and share it with different communities and generations.
